name: SPEYSIDE BOURBON COOPERAGE INC
same_company_evidence: Same company. Speyside Bourbon Cooperage Inc, grant address Jackson, Ohio 45640; the barrel maker is Ohio-based with stave mills in Virginia, which is where the layoffs are.
ohio_outcome: No closure or cut in Ohio found. The Jackson, Ohio cooperage is still running, and the company announced a $7.5 million Southeast Ohio investment in July 2023, after the 2022 grant. The layoffs were at the Smyth County, Virginia stave mill: 75 announced March 14, 2025 and 52 more announced March 3, 2026.
source: Cardinal News, March 3 2026 and March 14 2025; Virginia Business, March 4 2026; Chillicothe Gazette, July 1 2023; Business Journals, June 23 2021 (Google News RSS)
notes: The flagged headline is a Virginia plant. Jackson, Ohio was expanding over the same period.

name: AK STEEL CORPORATION
entity_filed: AK Steel Corporation, the grant payee, was acquired; no bankruptcy filing.
same_company_evidence: Same company. EIN 31-1267098, grant address West Chester, Ohio 45069, which is AK Steel's headquarters campus.
ohio_outcome: The grant payee stopped existing as an independent company the year after the grant. Cleveland-Cliffs agreed to buy AK Steel on Dec. 3, 2019 in a $1.1 billion stock deal, and AK Steel was delisted when the deal closed March 13, 2020. The West Chester headquarters building, the grant address, was listed for sale Oct. 8, 2024. The job losses in the flagged headlines were out of state: 260 at Ashland Works in Kentucky, closed January 2020, and more than 200 at Dearborn, Michigan in May 2020.
source: CNBC and Cleveland.com, Dec. 3 2019; Business Journals, March 13 2020 and Oct. 8 2024; WXYZ, May 4 2020; Northern Kentucky Tribune, Sept. 4 2019 (Google News RSS)
notes: This is a sale, not an insolvency. Counted here because the Ohio operation that got the grant was absorbed and its headquarters site was put on the market. No Ohio jobs figure found.

name: OWENS-BROCKWAY GLASS CONTAINER INC
same_company_evidence: Same company. EIN 22-2784144, grant address Zanesville, Ohio 43701, the O-I container plant in South Zanesville.
ohio_outcome: The Zanesville plant is still operating; the United Steelworkers wrote about it as a working factory in May 2024. The flagged closures were out of state: Streator, Illinois, more than 150 jobs, announced Oct. 23 2024, and Portland, Oregon, 90 jobs, announced July 30 2025. The one Ohio setback is money, not jobs: O-I began a Zanesville decarbonization project in January 2025 and the Department of Energy then terminated the $57.3 million award, reported June 3 2025.
source: Shaw Local, Oct. 23 and 27 2024; KGW, July 30 2025; United Steelworkers, May 6 2024; ESG Dive, Jan. 17 2025; Business Journals and Zanesville Times Recorder, June 3-4 2025 (Google News RSS)
notes: O-I also shut its Perrysburg, Ohio innovation center in October 2024, a separate site from the grant address.

name: OHIO UNIVERSITY
same_company_evidence: Same organization. Ohio University, Athens, Ohio 45701.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed that relates to the grant. The university shut its Pride Center, Women's Center and Multicultural Center on April 30 2025 to comply with a new state law, Senate Bill 1. The grants were economic development payments and the university is operating normally.
source: 10TV, April 30 2025 (Google News RSS)
notes: Headline is a policy story, not a business failure.

name: BIERY CHEESE CO
same_company_evidence: Same company. EIN 22-xxxx not needed: Biery Cheese is the family cheese packer headquartered in Louisville, Ohio; the Chicago grant address is a payment lockbox.
ohio_outcome: The Louisville, Ohio home plant is still running. The closure was in Wisconsin: the Plover plant, 104 jobs, announced Feb. 1 2023 and shut by the end of May 2023, the same year as the grant.
source: WAOW and WSAW, Feb. 1 2023; Point/Plover Metro Wire, Feb. 2 2023; Canton Repository and Akron Beacon Journal coverage of the Louisville, Ohio company (Google News RSS)
notes: Worth noting for the post that the grant year and the Wisconsin shutdown are the same year, but no Ohio jobs were lost.

name: Sauder Woodworking Co
same_company_evidence: Same company. Sauder Woodworking Co, Archbold, Ohio 43502, and the layoff stories name Archbold.
ohio_outcome: Sauder laid off about 150 workers at its Archbold, Ohio factory, announced Aug. 8 2025, which the company blamed on a sales decline. The plant stayed open; Sauder responded publicly on Aug. 12 2025.
source: WTOL, Aug. 8 2025; Woodworking Network, Aug. 8 2025; Bryan Times, Aug. 12 2025 (Google News RSS)
notes: Grants were 2015 and 2017, $100,000 each. The cut is eight years after the first grant.

name: Mohawk Fine Papers Inc
entity_filed: Mohawk Fine Papers Inc, the grant payee.
same_company_evidence: Same company. Mohawk Fine Papers Inc, grant address Ashtabula, Ohio 44004, and the closure stories name the Ashtabula mill.
ohio_outcome: The Ashtabula mill closed in February 2024, cutting 95 jobs. Fedrigoni bought certain Mohawk assets that same month, reported Feb. 23 2024, and Plastpro 2000 later acquired the Ashtabula facility itself, reported Nov. 15 2024.
source: Star Beacon, Feb. 15 2024; Business Journals, Feb. 22 2024; PaperAge, Feb. 23 2024; Packaging Dive, March 1 2024; Star Beacon, Nov. 15 2024 (Google News RSS)
notes: The clearest case in this batch: the grant site itself closed, eight years after a $200,000 grant.

name: AVELO AIRLINES INC
same_company_evidence: Same company. Avelo Airlines Inc, Houston, Texas. The project data in this repo ties the JobsOhio payments to Avelo's Dayton-Orlando route.
ohio_outcome: The Ohio service JobsOhio paid for ended. Avelo's Dayton to Orlando route flew from January 2023 to September 2023, nine months, 73 flights and about 9,555 passengers, against $200,000 paid in FY2023-24. Avelo did not fail: it launched Cleveland service in March 2026 after Frontier cuts and the Spirit exit.
source: data/air_service_routes.csv in this repo, built from DOT T-100; Business Journals and Spectrum News, March 18-19 2026; WRAL, Jan. 13 2026 (Google News RSS)
notes: Not a corporate failure. The flagged headline is about Raleigh-Durham and Wilmington bases. The Ohio finding is that the subsidized route was discontinued within the grant period.

name: Al Neyer LLC
same_company_evidence: Same company. Al. Neyer LLC, Cincinnati, Ohio, the design-build developer, renamed Merus in 2022.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed. The headline is a fundraising story: the firm closed, meaning finished raising, a $200 million private equity real estate development fund on Aug. 30 2022. The company is still operating in Cincinnati.
source: PR Newswire, Aug. 30 2022 (Google News RSS)
notes: The word "closes" in the headline means a fund close, the opposite of a failure.

name: ALPLA INC
same_company_evidence: Grant payee is ALPLA Inc, Lima, Ohio 45806. The flagged closure is not in Ohio: the Cortland Voice is a hyper-local outlet for Cortland County, New York, and the story describes a shared ALPLA and Voyant Beauty plant on Central Avenue in the City of Cortland, New York.
ohio_outcome: No Ohio closure or cut found. The Lima, Ohio plant turns up in no closure or layoff coverage, and ALPLA was still adding US capacity in 2026, including an $8 million blow molding plant in Las Vegas announced October 2026.
source: Cortland Voice, Aug. 23 2022, read via the Wayback Machine snapshot of Nov. 29 2023; Plastics News, Oct. 1 2026; Packaging Dive, Oct. 15 2026 (Google News RSS)
notes: Easy to mistake for Cortland, Ohio in Trumbull County. It is Cortland, New York.

name: CHARTER NEXT GENERATION INC
same_company_evidence: Same company. Charter Next Generation Inc, grant payment address Milton, Wisconsin; its Ohio operations are in Lexington and Ontario, Richland County.
ohio_outcome: Ohio grew rather than shrank. CNG announced an expansion in March and April 2025 slated to create 125 new jobs and finish in 2028, and in November 2025 said it would build a 456,000 square foot warehouse at the former GM plant in Ontario, Ohio. The September 2026 closure was a blown film plant in Texas.
source: Richland Source, March 31 and April 4 2025; Mansfield News Journal, Nov. 11 2025; Plastics News, Oct. 2 2026; Packaging Dive, Oct. 5 2026 (Google News RSS)
notes: Flagged headline is a packaging-industry roundup of closures elsewhere.

name: International Paper Company
same_company_evidence: Same company. International Paper Company, grant address Kenton, Ohio 43326.
ohio_outcome: No closure of the Kenton, Ohio grant site was found, and I could not positively confirm the site is still running either. International Paper did close an Ohio plant in the same stretch: the Marion, Ohio container plant, announced June 26 2025 and shut in September 2025, with more than 100 jobs lost. Marion is a separate site from the grant address. The flagged headlines cover closures in Georgia, California, Kentucky, Texas, New Jersey and Kansas.
source: 95.3 WKTN, June 26 2025; Marion Star, June 27 2025; Spectrum News and Marion County Now, June 30 2025; Packaging Dive, Aug. 21 2025, Nov. 12 2025 and June 29 2026 (Google News RSS)
notes: Unsettled piece: whether the 2016 grant paid for the Kenton plant or for the nearby Marion plant. Worth one check against the JobsOhio project announcement before the post names this one.

name: Klarna Inc
same_company_evidence: Same company. Klarna Inc, grant address Columbus, Ohio 43215, the Short North office that was Klarna's US base.
ohio_outcome: The Columbus operation was cut. Klarna cut 102 jobs, most of them in Columbus, announced Oct. 30 2023 and effective just before Christmas, as it outsourced customer service; about 500 jobs in total were transferred. Klarna listed Columbus as its US base in its IPO filing on Sept. 3 2025 and dropped that reference by Sept. 11 2025.
source: Business Journals, Oct. 30 2023, Sept. 3 2025 and Sept. 11 2025; Payments Dive, Nov. 2 2023 (Google News RSS)
notes: The flagged headline was a generic earnings story. The real Ohio cut is the 2023 outsourcing round, six years after a $125,000 grant.

name: Precision Products Group Inc
same_company_evidence: Different company. The grant went to Precision Products Group Inc of Apple Creek, Ohio 44606, a private-equity-backed industrial platform. The headline is about Kaman Precision Products, a unit of Kaman Corporation of Bloomfield, Connecticut, closing a bomb fuze plant in Orlando, Florida.
ohio_outcome: Nothing happened in Ohio. Precision Products Group was still buying companies after the grant, acquiring Saylor Technical Products in March 2023.
source: Business Journals, Jan. 31 2023; National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors, March 21 2023 (Google News RSS)
notes: Name collision on the words "Precision Products".

name: NEW HORIZONS BAKING COMPANY INC
same_company_evidence: Same company. New Horizons Baking Company Inc, grant address Norwalk, Ohio 44857, and the closure stories name the same Norwalk-based bakery.
ohio_outcome: An Ohio plant is closing. New Horizons said on Jan. 16 2026 that it will shut its north Toledo plant in March 2026, with 68 permanent layoffs. That is the plant it announced a $13 million expansion for in May 2023. The Norwalk headquarters plant, the grant address, is still operating; OSHA proposed $394,849 in penalties against it in December 2025.
source: WTOL and WTVG, Jan. 16 2026; Food Business News, Jan. 21 2026; Cleveland.com, Jan. 22 2026; Toledo Blade, May 9 2023; WKYC, Dec. 16 2025 (Google News RSS)
notes: The closed site is Toledo, not the Norwalk grant address, but both are Ohio operations of the grantee.

name: The Home Depot Inc
same_company_evidence: Same company. The Home Depot Inc, grant payment address Atlanta, Georgia 30339.
ohio_outcome: Nothing found in Ohio. The flagged story is a small round of corporate layoffs at the Atlanta headquarters in June 2023.
source: 11Alive, June 16 2023 (Google News RSS)
notes: Routine corporate news.

name: Downtown Cleveland Alliance
same_company_evidence: Different entity in the headline. The grant payee is the Downtown Cleveland Alliance, Cleveland, Ohio 44115, which got $50,000 in 2015 for conference expense support. The closure was Tower City Cinemas, a movie theater tenant in Tower City Center.
ohio_outcome: The Alliance is still operating. It renamed itself Downtown Cleveland, Inc. in June 2023 and was still running downtown safety and public space programs as of February 2026.
source: News 5 Cleveland, Aug. 31 2020; Cleveland.com, June 14 2023; Cleveland Magazine, Feb. 16 2026 (Google News RSS)
notes: The theater closure is a tenant, not the grantee.

name: FedEx Supply Chain Inc
same_company_evidence: Same company. FedEx Supply Chain Inc, grant address Columbus, Ohio 43217, the Rickenbacker area. The Ohio closure stories name FedEx Supply Chain and the city of Lima.
ohio_outcome: An Ohio operation closed. FedEx Supply Chain stopped running the Procter & Gamble distribution center at 635 N. Cool Rd. in Lima, Ohio and laid off 63 workers by Oct. 31 2025, after P&G switched logistics providers; the notice was reported Sept. 4 2025. FedEx then agreed to sell the whole FedEx Supply Chain unit to CMA CGM for $1.4 billion, reported July 1 2026. No closure of the Columbus grant address itself was found.
source: Business Journals and LimaOhio.com, Sept. 4 2025; FreightWaves, Sept. 5 2025 and July 1 2026; Supply Chain Dive, March 28 2022 and Sept. 8 2025 (Google News RSS)
notes: Two separate things here: a 63-job Ohio closure in 2025, and the sale of the business unit in 2026. The flagged headline was about Memphis.

name: AIR WISCONSIN AIRLINES LLC
entity_filed: Air Wisconsin Airlines LLC, operating subsidiary of Harbor Diversified, Inc. No bankruptcy filing found.
same_company_evidence: Same company. Air Wisconsin Airlines LLC, grant payment address Appleton, Wisconsin, subsidiary of Harbor Diversified, which reported 1,308 full-time employees in its 2019 10-K.
ohio_outcome: The carrier stopped flying. Air Wisconsin warned of layoffs affecting more than 500 people on Jan. 31 2025 after ending its American Airlines contract, planned another round of more than 100 in April 2025, halted scheduled flights in early April 2025, withdrew from a $10 million Essential Air Service contract in September 2025, and sold its operating assets and fleet in February 2026. Its Ohio activity in DOT T-100 data was Dayton- and Columbus-based regional and charter flying, which ended with the airline. No Ohio site tied to the $50,000 grant was identified.
source: WPR, Jan. 31 and April 11 2025; Simple Flying, Feb. 2 2025; AirlineGeeks, April 4 and Sept. 9 2025; Post-Crescent, Feb. 3 2026; Business Journals, Feb. 12 2026; DOT T-100 files in data/raw/t100 (Google News RSS)
notes: Confirmed at the company level. What the Ohio grant actually paid for is still unknown, so the Ohio link is inferred, not sourced.

name: PPG INDUSTRIES INC
same_company_evidence: Same company. PPG Industries Inc, grant address Barberton, Ohio 44203, which is PPG's silicas plant site; the Ohio EPA covered a wastewater leak on PPG land in Barberton in March 2024.
ohio_outcome: The Ohio operation was sold off. PPG agreed on Aug. 29 2024 to sell its silicas products business to Qemetica for $310 million, and the deal completed in late November 2024. Barberton is explicitly part of it: Qemetica took over the silicas manufacturing operations at Barberton, Ohio and the R&D operations at Monroeville, Pennsylvania under lease from PPG, along with owned plants in Lake Charles, Louisiana and Delfzijl, Netherlands. The business has about 400 employees across all sites; no Barberton-only figure was given. The flagged closure, Worwag Coatings in Lafayette, Indiana, 54 jobs, September 2022, was out of state.
source: CHEManager, Sept. 1 2024, which lists the sites; Manufacturing Dive, Sept. 6 2024; BIC Magazine, Nov. 29 2024; Akron Beacon Journal, March 6 2024; Journal & Courier, Jan. 20 2022 (Google News RSS)
notes: A divestiture four years after a $50,000 grant, not an insolvency. The plant kept running under a new owner.
